card.title: Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor Land Takings

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor-I (P114338), US$975 million loan approved 31 May 2011; with EDFC-2 (US$1.1 billion) and EDFC-3 (US$650 million) it financed three sections of the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor: Ludhiana-Khurja, Khurja-Kanpur and Kanpur-Mughal Sarai.

companies.name: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India (DFCCIL)
companies.role: State railway company that borrowed, built the line and ran land acquisition with state revenue officers
companies.desc: An Indian state railway company, a special purpose vehicle registered on 30 October 2006 under the Companies Act 1956 and reporting to the Ministry of Railways, which holds all its equity. It plans, finances, builds, maintains and operates India's Dedicated Freight Corridors: the Eastern corridor of 1,840 route km and the Western corridor of 1,502 route km.

card.community: Across the three loans, nearly 85,000 people in about 1,000 villages in four states were affected by land acquisition (4,336 hectares). The World Bank reports many complaints from people paid lower rates used before India's 2013 land law raised compensation, and unrest over unpaid or late compensation that disrupted construction in some places. Some families went to court seeking the better terms given to 265 neighbouring households. In Chandauli, farmers in Cheeto village held a sit-in from 25 February 2016, and CPI (ML) Liberation workers began a hunger strike on 11 July 2016. They said promised jobs, market-price compensation and rehabilitation were not given.
card.displaced_note: About 85,000 project-affected people across EDFC-1, 2 and 3 (World Bank); ICIJ estimated 46,646 displaced for EDFC-1. Neither figure is a count of people who lost homes.
card.outcome: The IEG review of EDFC-1 says no land acquisition issues were pending at closing. The World Bank reports that affected families below the poverty line fell from 63% to 23%. The Khurja-Dadri stretch was left out of further Bank financing over concerns about meeting the Bank's resettlement rules and was finished with government money. In the impact assessment survey for EDFC-1, 40% of affected men and 50% of affected women said they were satisfied with the compensation and resettlement help (World Bank, 2024).
card.confidence_note: The World Bank's report records complaints about lower payments and unrest over unpaid compensation, and farmers protested in Chandauli; the protest claims come from a political party and were not independently checked in the press report. The Bank says all land issues were settled by closing and that poverty among affected families fell. No independent count of people left worse off was found. An earlier entry on the industrial corridor was dropped for documenting no harm from the railway itself.

card.whole: By the World Bank's own count, its Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor projects built about 1,200 km of new track between 2011 and 2024. On the first section, daily freight capacity rose from 32 train pairs to over 130, freight trains run at three times the speed of ordinary services, and daily passenger services on the Khurja-Kanpur line rose from 69 to 128 as freight moved off it. The Bank reports about 55,000 tonnes of CO2 avoided in 2024 and about 9 million days of work during construction. No independent check of these figures was found.
card.conditions: The 2011 EDFC-I loan (Loan 8066-IN) required the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation to carry out the project in line with its Resettlement Action Plan, Resettlement Policy Framework and environmental plans, to set up district grievance committees and an Ombudsman by 30 September 2011, and to review and update the resettlement plan each year with the Bank. The loan agreement also required India to have a Bank-approved resettlement action plan in place before civil works began on linked road overbridges in Uttar Pradesh, and to sign a concession agreement between the Railways Ministry and the corporation on terms satisfactory to the Bank (World Bank, Loan Agreement and Project Agreement, 2011).

card.title: Homes demolished without compensation on the North Buckingham canal in Nagapattinam
card.place: Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu, India, with resettlement sites at Okkiyum-Thuraipakkam and north Chennai

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Emergency Tsunami Reconstruction Project, project number P094513, credit IDA-40540, approved 3 May 2005 after the December 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, effective 9 August 2005, closing extended from 30 April 2008 to 31 December 2011. US$235.0 million of the credit was cancelled because the closing date was not extended further. The completion report of 18 June 2012 rates the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Unsatisfactory and borrower performance Moderately Unsatisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group rates the outcome Unsatisfactory against both the original and the revised objectives (ICR Review, 29 May 2013).

companies.name: Commissioner of Revenue Administration, Revenue Administration, Disaster Management and Mitigation Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
companies.role: Lead implementing agency named in the completion report, the state department that runs disaster relief and holds the district collectors under it. Thirteen implementing agencies carried out procurement; the Tamil Nadu Slum Clearance Board held the urban housing and the transit accommodation. No construction contractor is named for the canal works.
companies.desc: The head office of the revenue arm of the government of Tamil Nadu in India, working in each district through the District Collector. The Board of Revenue was abolished during 1980 and its functions taken over by three new commissionerates, now five; the department keeps land records and handles mutations, issues certificates such as community, income and legal heirship certificates, acts as custodian of government property, and distributes relief in disasters.

card.community: The completion report records that in Nagapattinam district, work to improve the North Buckingham canal ran ahead of the state's resettlement and rehabilitation policy: the local authorities demolished the affected structures without offering compensation and assistance. After the Bank's team learned of it, the Government of Tamil Nadu drew up retrofit measures and put them in place, and all six displaced families were offered cash grants for the impacts they had suffered. Five families had received the grant when the credit closed on 31 December 2011 and the state was still in the process of paying the sixth. At two resettlement sites built for tsunami-affected people, about 100 families of the existing host population were affected: at Okkiyum-Thuraipakkam all 29 host families were moved temporarily into nearby Slum Clearance Board housing to wait for permanent houses, and at the All India Radio site in north Chennai 60 of 70 families had shifted by the closing date, leaving 10 families in temporary shelter awaiting a permanent site. For the resettlement sites as a whole, 560 hectares of land was acquired, 330 hectares of it private land, bought by private negotiation under a special government order letting district collectors set compensation at up to 200 per cent of guideline or registered values; about 40 hectares was donated by local citizens. The completion report says state funds, not Bank funds, paid for that land. The Independent Evaluation Group records that the project team told it the project was in compliance with the resettlement policy at the time the completion report was written, and that the 100 families physically displaced in Tamil Nadu were either given alternative housing or were expected to be shortly; that is a statement by Bank staff, not a document.
card.killed_note: The completion report gives tsunami death and injury figures for the disaster itself, not for the project: 5,792 people reported missing and 6,913 injured in one passage, and 3,504 injured with 472,000 dislocated in another. Those are the disaster's toll and nothing in the documents attributes any death to the works.
card.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 360 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved.
card.outcome: The credit closed on 31 December 2011 without a further extension, with one of the six Nagapattinam families still waiting for its grant and 10 host families at the north Chennai site still in temporary shelter. The completion report lists the difficulty of decommissioning and demolishing transit shelters, and unwillingness among beneficiaries to accept temporary relocation, among the lessons of in-situ urban resettlement.
card.confidence_note: The demolition without compensation is stated plainly in the Bank's completion report and repeated in the Independent Evaluation Group's review, but both are the lender's own documents and neither names the stretch of canal or the village. No Indian press report, court record or audit of this demolition was found. The completion report does not say which component financed the North Buckingham canal works; it records the demolition in the project's own social safeguards section. The report also does not say whether the sixth family was ever paid.

sources.title: India - Emergency Tsunami Reconstruction Project (ETRP): Implementation Completion and Results Report (P094513)

Mission
sources.publisher: Commissionerate of Revenue Administration and Disaster Management, Government of Tamil Nadu

card.whole: The credit was to rebuild housing and to put in evacuation shelters, evacuation routes and early warning systems in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry after the December 2004 tsunami. By the completion report's own count, 4,121 houses were finished to disaster-resistant standards, 29 per cent of the revised target of 14,370, and in Puducherry about 550 of the 1,752 houses taken into the project were finished. The same report records that no evacuation shelter was built against a revised target of 140, that no early warning system was installed against a revised target of 439, and that evacuation route works had not started when the credit closed. These figures are the lender's own; no independent count was found.
card.conditions: The conformed project agreement for Credit 4054-IN required Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry to carry out the project in accordance with an environmental and social management framework, and, before any project activity, to screen for adverse environmental and social impacts, prepare mitigation plans satisfactory to the Association and implement them (Schedule 2, paragraph 8(a) and (b)). The same paragraph required each state, "prior to any relocation of people to new areas involving involuntary resettlement", to prepare resettlement plans satisfactory to the Association and implement them, and, "prior to any acquisition of private land for the purpose of implementing the Project, pay compensation to the owners of such land in accordance with the provisions of the ESMF" (paragraph 8(d) and (e)). Where tsunami-affected people were moved to new areas, the states could not carry out that work unless, "to the extent practicable", the land was state-owned and free of encumbrances and encroachments or had been obtained voluntarily (paragraph 8(c)).

card.title: Lucknow-Muzaffarpur National Highway: 442 hectares taken from 23,394 landholders
card.place: NH-28 between Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh and Muzaffarpur, Bihar, India

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-47640 for the Lucknow-Muzaffarpur National Highway Project (P077856). US$620 million approved 21 December 2004, effective 28 December 2005, closing moved from 30 June 2010 to 30 June 2012, US$615.70 million disbursed. Implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 13 December 2012).

card.community: The Bank's completion report describes the project's displacement and resettlement impacts as 'high in magnitude as well as intensity' and counts the taking of 442 hectares of private land from about 14,976 titleholders and 8,418 people without title, and 259 religious properties. It says that by the closing date land acquisition and resettlement were fully completed and all affected families had received their compensation and main entitlements, except a few whose cases were in court over who owned the land. Four religious properties could not be moved because religious leaders took hard positions. Stretches of land totalling up to 1,800 metres were taken out of the project because ownership disputes took too long to settle; the highways authority said it would do that work with its own money. Over the life of the project the Bank's own ratings for resettlement implementation moved from satisfactory to unsatisfactory and back to satisfactory. The consultants who were to evaluate what happened to resettled people at the end of the project were not hired until the closing date, so that evaluation was still under way; the Independent Evaluation Group says the Bank would keep monitoring it until the final report was submitted. The Independent Evaluation Group notes that the completion report does not state that all safeguards were met or complied with. At stakeholder workshops the general view reported was that land acquisition and resettlement 'was done reasonably well except for a few stray cases of dissatisfaction', and that landowners along the road were pleased because their asset values had risen; many people at the same workshops said road safety had worsened because of higher speeds.
card.suppression: No arrests, forced evictions or police action are recorded in the Bank's completion report or the Independent Evaluation Group review.
card.killed_note: No deaths are recorded in the Bank's completion report or the Independent Evaluation Group review.
card.displaced_note: 442 hectares of private land taken from about 14,976 titleholders and 8,418 people without title, per the World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report of 13 December 2012; 23,394 is the sum of the report's two figures. The report does not say how many people lost a home as against part of a field or a roadside pitch. ICIJ's 'Evicted and Abandoned' table gives 75,434, listed as an estimate of people displaced and taken from World Bank project documents as of 31 December 2014.
card.outcome: The Bank rated the project's outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory and its own performance Moderately Unsatisfactory. Land acquisition, tree cutting and utility shifting delayed the works and the project was restructured in May 2010 and June 2012, with contracts 9 to 12 taken out of it. Environmental compliance in the early years is described as patchy and moved from satisfactory to unsatisfactory before returning to satisfactory. At the time of the report the Bank was still monitoring clean-up work in some sections and camps, drainage issues on contracts 1 to 3, and drainage, slope protection and debris clearance on the Gorakhpur bypass, which the Bank did not fund but monitored as a linked project. The end-of-project study of what happened to resettled people had not been completed when the completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review were written.
card.confidence_note: This is a large land taking that the Bank's own documents record as finished with compensation paid, not a record of a failure. The gaps in the record are that the Bank's rating for resettlement implementation fell to unsatisfactory at points during the project, that the consultants who were to assess what happened to resettled people were not hired until the closing date so that no completed assessment exists, and that the Independent Evaluation Group states the completion report does not say safeguards were met and complied with. An unmeasured outcome is not a measured harm, and none is claimed here. No press report, court record or NGO field research on this corridor's resettlement was found, and the only account of how affected people felt is the stakeholder workshop summary inside the Bank's own report. The lender is reporting on its own project.

sources.title: India - Lucknow-Muzaffarpur National Highway Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report
ICR Review: India - Lucknow Muzaffarpur National Highway Project (P077856)
Evicted and Abandoned: Lucknow-Muzaffarpur National Highway Project (P077856)

card.whole: By the World Bank's own count, 328 km of NH-28 were upgraded to a four-lane divided road, after the length was cut from the 483 km planned at approval. Travel time fell 23 per cent for cars and 25 per cent for trucks against a 20 per cent target, and fatal accidents across the corridor fell 36 per cent against a 10 per cent target; the 10 per cent cut targeted in truck operating costs was reached in none of the three sections, and on the Ayodhya-Gorakhpur section fatal accidents rose from 22 in the 2002 baseline year to 43. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 26.2 per cent for the 327 km finally built, against 26 per cent estimated at appraisal for the full 483 km; it counts savings in vehicle operating costs and in travel time for passengers and goods, and leaves accident savings out. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group rated the outcome Unsatisfactory and Bank performance Unsatisfactory, each a step below the completion report's rating, and rated the quality of the project's monitoring Negligible. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
card.conditions: The project was environmental category A. Entitlements were to be delivered under a resettlement action plan for each phase, under the Bank's resettlement policy of the time, operational directive 3.40. The Bank agreed to keep monitoring resettlement on corridor sections it did not finance until they were finished, under the project's resettlement policy and the project agreement.
card.ecosystem: Trees were cut along the corridor and compensatory planting was carried out. The completion report records drainage problems on contracts 1 to 3 and drainage, slope protection and debris clearance problems on the Gorakhpur bypass still open at closing, and says borrow areas were rehabilitated as farmland and ponds.

card.title: Dehlon Bypass Built Over a Disputed Plot, Punjab
card.place: Dehlon bypass, Ludhiana district, Punjab, India

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-48430 for the Punjab State Road Sector Project (P090585). US$250 million approved 5 December 2006; US$248,110,727.51 disbursed against a total project cost of US$407.3 million. Original closing 5 June 2012; the project was restructured at level 2 in August 2012 and again on 10 November 2014, and closed 5 June 2017, five years late. Environmental Category A, with the policies on environmental assessment, forests, physical cultural resources and involuntary resettlement triggered (IEG ICR Review, 8 May 2018; World Bank Project Appraisal Document, 10 November 2006).

card.community: At Dehlon, where the project built a bypass, one of the owners of a plot refused the compensation offered in May 2017 and filed a case in the High Court; a complaint had already gone to the Bank's Grievance Redress Service in December 2016. In April 2017 the contractors tried to start work on the plot and the Bank team insisted all work stop until compensation was settled. Soon after the project closed on 5 June 2017 the contractor went back onto the plot and finished building the bypass. The plaintiff did not appear at the High Court hearing of 31 January 2018 and the hearing was rescheduled for the end of March 2018. The Bank's task team leader told the Independent Evaluation Group that half of the co-owners have been paid, that the co-owner who complained is still pursuing the matter in the High Court, and that the matter has not been resolved. There was also a built harm from the drainage works: in 2009 the project team found that drains built in urban areas sat above the plinth level of the buildings next to them, blocking numerous commercial and residential entrances. The Independent Evaluation Group attributes this to weak monitoring and to the roads board's environment and social officers not being involved in two upgrading works, which were closed out without proper clean-up, rehabilitation or compliance reports, and to inadequate handling of the environmental management plan and work-site safety on the output and performance based road contract. The Bank team later arranged an assessment and an action plan to remedy it. At appraisal the project expected 112 people from 24 households to be marginally or temporarily affected on the rehabilitation roads with none displaced, and about 31 hectares of land to be acquired. For the upgrading roads the appraisal document gives two readings of the same impact: its main text says 4,731 people from 1,233 households would be affected at least temporarily with people from 197 households expected to be displaced, while its safeguards annex, para 10.9, says 4,731 persons would be affected from 831 households of which 1,233 would be displaced from 197 households. Both are appraisal expectations, not outcomes.
card.killed_note: Two fatal workplace accidents happened in 2016. The Independent Evaluation Group's review records them in one sentence, citing para 66 of the completion report: 'there were two fatal workplace accidents in 2016 which were not reported to the Bank'. The Bank's team learned of them only after making a specific request to the Punjab Roads and Bridges Development Board in February 2017, and then met contractors, consultants and the board about construction zone safety and traffic management. No document opened states that the accidents happened on works financed by the project, names the dead, gives the dates or locations, says which contractor's works they occurred on, or records any compensation to their families. They are therefore left uncounted.
card.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 3,977 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The appraisal document's main-text figure for people affected at least temporarily on the upgrading roads is 4,731, with people from 197 households expected to be displaced; its safeguards annex gives 1,233 as the number displaced instead. No Bank document found gives a count of people actually relocated.
card.outcome: The loan closed on 5 June 2017. The bypass across the disputed plot was completed after closing. The Bank's task team leader told the Independent Evaluation Group that half the co-owners have been paid, that the co-owner who objected has not been, and that the case continues in the High Court, with the team still following the matter up as of the review of 8 May 2018. No later account was found.
card.confidence_note: The Dehlon sequence, the two fatal accidents and the blocked entrances all come from the Independent Evaluation Group's review of the Bank's completion report, which cites that report paragraph by paragraph. The completion report itself is not disclosed in the Bank's document archive for this project: a search of all 62 documents listed for P090585, and two separate title searches of the Bank's document archive, return only the Independent Evaluation Group's review. The lender is therefore the only source, and on the state of the compensation it is the Bank's own task team leader speaking to the evaluators rather than a document. Nobody is named except by role, the drains that blocked 'numerous' entrances are not counted, and the two deaths are recorded in one sentence with no detail at all.

card.whole: The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 8 May 2018 records 711 km of road upgraded, rehabilitated or maintained, against an original target of 700 km, 347 accident black spots improved, and the Dehlon bypass completed. Average speed on the state's Plan Road network rose from 34.2 km an hour in 2006 to 47.6 km an hour in 2017, close to the revised target of 48. Project roads in poor condition fell from 67 per cent in 2006 to 1.4 per cent in 2012 and then rose to 31.6 per cent in 2017 as rehabilitation and maintenance backlogs built up. Vehicle operating costs were measured only on the roads the project worked on: they rose 10 per cent on the rehabilitated roads and 11 per cent on the periodic-maintenance roads, and fell nearly 24 per cent on the roads held under output and performance-based contracts, against a 20 per cent target. On the project's road safety indicator the review records no improvement: fatal accidents on the Plan Road network rose from 2,655 in 2005 to 5,077 in 2016, then fell about 15 per cent to about 4,278 in 2017. Rates of return recalculated after the works were 31.8 per cent for upgrading, 28.5 per cent for rehabilitation and 50.4 per cent for periodic maintenance, against appraisal estimates of 36.5, 44.2 and 58.4 per cent; the review cites the completion report's explanation that capital costs rose, works were delayed and traffic grew more slowly than forecast. The review rates efficiency substantial and the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory. The completion report is not disclosed, the figures are the lender's own, and no independent check was found.
card.conditions: The project was environmental category A and triggered four safeguard policies: environmental assessment, physical cultural resources, forests and involuntary resettlement. A Resettlement and Rehabilitation Policy Framework with an entitlement matrix was adopted, and resettlement action plans were completed and disclosed for the first phase of roads before appraisal. Two covenants governed the land. The Government of Punjab was to ensure that works were carried out in line with the framework and the plans, and that neither was revised or set aside without the Bank's prior approval. It was also not to begin any civil works at an affected site until the physical relocation of people at that site had been completed to the Bank's satisfaction, with relocation on all first-phase roads to be finished before 5 June 2008 (Project Appraisal Document, 10 November 2006). The implementing agency was the Punjab Roads and Bridges Development Board.
